title_en: The life of this world like rain
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. A parable or similitude is not a dated event and is not placed in any order: the chapter states only what the ayat present as a similitude, what it is likened to, and what the ayat themselves say. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

chapters.title_en: The life of this world like rain

claims.statement_en: The ayah says that the similitude of the life of this world is like water that God sent down from the sky, with which the plants of the earth, from which people and cattle eat, mingled, until the earth took its adornment and was adorned, and its people thought they were able over it, then His command came to it by night or by day, and He made it a reaped field, as if it had not been there the day before.
The ayah adds that thus God makes the signs clear for a people who reflect.

The ayah commands that a similitude of the life of this world be struck for them: like water that God sent down from the sky, with which the plants of the earth mingled, and it became dry stubble that the winds scatter; and God has power over all things.

The ayah says to know that the life of this world is play, amusement, adornment, boasting among you and rivalry in wealth and children, like a rain whose growth pleased the kuffar; then it dries, and you see it yellow, then it becomes broken stubble.
The ayah adds that in the hereafter there is severe punishment and forgiveness from God and approval, and that the life of this world is only the enjoyment of delusion.

chapters.summary_md: The ayat in different surahs liken the life of this world to rain and to what grows from it, which then becomes a reaped field, dry stubble or broken stubble [c1][c3][c4]. The last of them adds that in the hereafter there is severe punishment and forgiveness from God and approval [c5].
chapters.body_md:
In one ayah, the similitude of the life of this world is like water that God sent down from the sky, with which the plants of the earth mingled [c1]. The earth took its adornment and was adorned, and its people thought they were able over it, then His command came to it by night or by day, and He made it a reaped field, as if it had not been there the day before [c1]. Thus God makes the signs clear for a people who reflect [c2].

In another ayah, a similitude of the life of this world is to be struck for them, like water that God sent down from the sky, with which the plants of the earth mingled [c3]. It became dry stubble that the winds scatter, and God has power over all things [c3].

In a further ayah, the life of this world is play, amusement, adornment, boasting among you and rivalry in wealth and children [c4]. It is like a rain whose growth pleased the kuffar; then it dries, and you see it yellow, then it becomes broken stubble [c4]. In the hereafter there is severe punishment and forgiveness from God and approval, and the life of this world is only the enjoyment of delusion [c5].
chapters.deep_md: The ayat share the picture of water from the sky and the plants that grow with it, and each ends it differently: a reaped field, dry stubble scattered by the winds, and broken stubble [c1][c3][c4]. Only 10:24 and 18:45 speak of a similitude by that word, while 57:20 compares the life of this world to rain with the word like and lists what it is [c1][c3][c4]. The word kuffar in 57:20 is read as the disbelievers or as the farmers, and the ayah does not settle it [c4].
chapters.kids_md: The ayat say that the life of this world is like rain from the sky, and like the plants that grow with it [c1][c3]. The plants later become dry stubble [c3]. God has power over all things [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayat compare the life of this world to rain and to what grows from it, which then dries and is scattered or broken [c1][c3][c4]. Another reading is that the last ayah sets the life of this world beside the hereafter, where there is severe punishment and forgiveness from God and approval [c5].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: whether the ayat are statements of one similitude or separate similitudes; they come from different surahs and the ayat do not say.
- Not established: when the reaping or the drying takes place; 10:24 says by night or by day, and no more.
- The word kuffar in 57:20 is read as disbelievers or as farmers; this draft keeps the Arabic word.
- The ayat 10:24 and 18:45 use the word for a similitude (mathal); 57:20 gives a likeness with the word like and states what the life of this world is.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: none identified; a scholar should say whether any should be linked to these ayat.
The sense of kuffar in 57:20 and the wording of zukhruf (adornment) in 10:24 are for a scholar to decide.
